bug_description.original: Heap-based buffer overflow (out-of-bounds read) in PackLinuxElf64::elf_lookup (p_lx_elf.cpp). While processing crafted/malformed ELF string table data, strcmp can read past the end of the mapped file buffer, causing a one-byte heap read beyond the allocation. This can crash UPX or lead to memory disclosure when handling malicious ELF files.
bug_description.normalized: Malformed ELF64 DT_STRSZ and DT_STRTAB metadata can describe a dynamic string table whose claimed extent is not fully validated against its base address and terminating NUL, allowing get_str_name to return a dynstr pointer that strcmp reads past the mapped file buffer.

source.description: The PT_DYNAMIC parser materializes the attacker-controlled DT_STRSZ value as strtab_max, the claimed length of the dynamic string table.
source.value_from: ELF PT_DYNAMIC entries in the attacker-supplied file copied into file_image

root_cause.description: The fix adds the missing obligation that the DT_STRTAB base and DT_STRSZ extent stay within file_image and that the last byte of the claimed string table is a NUL terminator; the vulnerable code failed to enforce this combined bound-and-terminator condition before later string lookups.

sink.description: elf_lookup compares the requested symbol name against the dynstr entry pointer returned through get_dynsym_name/get_str_name, and strcmp keeps reading p until it finds a NUL byte beyond the mapped buffer.

tainted_value_origin.description: The entire attacker-controlled ELF file is copied into file_image, from which PT_DYNAMIC metadata, DT_STRTAB, and DT_SYMTAB contents are later read.

parser_admitted.description: The PoC is admitted as a 64-bit ET_DYN ELF object, which enters PT_DYNAMIC parsing and later the dynamic symbol-name lookup path.

fine_trace.note: Reads the attacker-controlled DT_STRSZ table index from the parsed PT_DYNAMIC metadata.
Uses that DT_STRSZ entry index to load the claimed dynamic-string-table size into strtab_max.
Reads the attacker-controlled DT_STRTAB table index that names which dynamic entry holds the string-table base address.
Loads from the selected DT_STRTAB entry the claimed file offset of the dynamic string table into strtab_beg.

This is the missing validation obligation named by the patch: the vulnerable path continues without proving that the DT_STRTAB base plus DT_STRSZ extent stays inside file_image and that the last byte of that range is a NUL terminator.
After invert_pt_dynamic returns, PackLinuxElf64help1 resolves DT_STRTAB into the dynstr base pointer that later name lookups index from.
get_dynsym_name extracts the current dynamic symbol's attacker-controlled st_name offset and passes that concrete value into get_str_name.

The patched-source safety check compares st_name only with the claimed DT_STRSZ-derived strtab_max; if st_name is below that length, the code still does not prove the referenced string is NUL-terminated before the end of file_image.
On the non-throwing path, get_str_name returns dynstr + st_name as p, carrying forward a pointer into the claimed string table without proving a terminating NUL exists before the mapped buffer ends.

elf_lookup compares the requested name against p; because the earlier DT_STRTAB/DT_STRSZ validation did not guarantee a NUL within the mapped buffer, strcmp continues reading p into the ASan-reported heap redzone.

format.name: malformed ELF64 shared object with mismatched DT_STRSZ limit and DT_STRTAB contents
format.contract: A single ELF64 ET_DYN file whose PT_DYNAMIC metadata makes UPX load a nonzero DT_STRSZ extent that passes the weak file_size-based check, resolves DT_STRTAB, and later returns a dynstr entry used during JNI_OnLoad lookup that lacks a terminating NUL before the end of file_image.
